questions.stem: Political power may best be defined as the ability to

options.text: control the behaviour of others, whether or not they consent
win an election in a free and fair contest
interpret the provisions of the constitution
advise government on matters of public policy

questions.explanation: Power is a capacity, and it is defined without reference to consent. A dictator who has never faced an election still exercises power, which is exactly why power alone is not enough to make a government rightful.

distractorRationale.b: Winning an election is one way of acquiring authority, but power can be seized without any election
distractorRationale.c: Interpreting the constitution is the specific function of the judiciary, not a definition of power
distractorRationale.d: Advising government describes influence, which carries no ability to compel

questions.stem: The main difference between power and authority is that authority

options.text: is always backed by superior military force
is recognised as rightful, so obedience to it is voluntary
can only be exercised by an elected official
cannot be lost once it has been acquired

questions.explanation: Legitimacy is the dividing line. Both power and authority can secure compliance, but authority secures it because the subjects accept the command as rightful, so force becomes the exception rather than the rule.

distractorRationale.a: Reliance on force is characteristic of raw power; authority reduces the need for force
distractorRationale.c: A hereditary Emir and an appointed judge both hold authority without being elected
distractorRationale.d: Authority is lost when the officeholder is impeached, defeated, retired or dismissed

questions.stem: A newly elected Local Government Chairman orders the closure of an illegal dump site and residents comply. The authority he is exercising is
questions.explanation: Residents obey because the Constitution and the electoral process placed him in an office empowered to give that directive. Authority of this kind belongs to the office rather than the person, so it passes to his successor.

distractorRationale.a: Traditional authority rests on inherited custom, as with an Emir or an Oba, not on election
distractorRationale.b: Charismatic authority rests on the leader's personal magnetism, which is irrelevant here
distractorRationale.d: Coercion is a form of power rather than a Weberian type of authority

questions.stem: The authority exercised by an Emir or an Oba over his subjects is classified by Max Weber as
questions.explanation: The stool is inherited and its commands are accepted because they have been accepted for generations. Custom and lineage, not statute or personality, supply the legitimacy.

distractorRationale.a: Legal-rational authority derives from written rules and formal office, such as a governor's
distractorRationale.c: Charismatic authority depends on personal qualities and dies with the individual
distractorRationale.d: Delegated authority is authority passed down from a superior officer, which is a different classification

questions.stem: A retired statesman who holds no public office persuades the National Assembly to amend a bill. He is exercising
questions.explanation: He can persuade but cannot command, and the legislators face no penalty for ignoring him. That is the defining mark of influence rather than authority.

distractorRationale.a: Authority requires a recognised right to issue binding directives, which a private citizen lacks
distractorRationale.b: Sovereignty is the supreme law-making power of the state as a whole
distractorRationale.d: Legislative power belongs to the National Assembly itself, not to the person advising it

questions.stem: Charismatic authority is generally regarded as the least stable type of authority because it

options.text: is never accepted by the followers of the leader
attaches to the personal qualities of an individual rather than to an office
is always acquired through the use of military force
is expressly forbidden by most written constitutions

questions.explanation: Because followers obey the person and not the position, there is no rule for succession. When the charismatic leader dies, is discredited or withdraws, the authority evaporates instead of passing to a successor.

distractorRationale.a: Charismatic authority is in fact enthusiastically accepted; that acceptance is its whole basis
distractorRationale.c: Charisma works through devotion and persuasion, not through arms
distractorRationale.d: Constitutions regulate offices; they neither create nor prohibit personal magnetism

questions.stem: A person may possess power without possessing authority.
questions.explanation: True. An armed gang or a leader who seizes government by coup can compel obedience while having no recognised right to do so. Power is capacity; authority is capacity plus legitimacy.

distractorRationale.b: This assumes the two always travel together, which would make every illegitimate regime impossible

questions.stem: A large employer threatens to withdraw investment from a state unless a proposed levy is dropped. The type of power being exercised is
questions.explanation: The lever being used is wealth and the jobs it creates, not weapons or statute. Control over investment and employment is the classic form of economic power in politics.

distractorRationale.a: Coercive power operates through force or the threat of physical harm
distractorRationale.c: Legislative power is the power to enact law, which belongs to the legislature being pressured
distractorRationale.d: Traditional power derives from custom and lineage, not from business assets
